answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must register identities by committing cryptographic stake burning governed by quadratic pricing: establishing the $n$-th alias burns $k \cdot n^2$ tokens. A malicious swarm attempting to build a cedar sanctuary finds its budget hollow, as superlinear burn requirements enforce punishing economic friction across the network landscape, turning an attacker's expansion into an insurmountable dune of wasted capital.
